patch.value: Budget recovery can recommend a smaller ceiling than the request that already truncated

A live unbounded contract inspection of 'pm contracts --command update --flags-only --json' showed an output_budget_truncation receipt with budget_source=default and budget_tokens=4500, restore_with='Increase --output-budget because no declared row collection can be continued', but recovery.cli='--output-budget 1200' and recovery_budget_multiplier=1. The prescribed retry is smaller than the effective budget that already omitted data, so an agent following the recovery can loop or lose more context. Define one SDK recovery-budget contract that is monotonic relative to the effective request and executable across every non-resumable bounded surface.

Recovery budgets are computed from the effective post-precedence budget and are strictly greater than it whenever the instruction says increase; the next budget is derived from measured encoded cost with documented rounding and safety margin, never from a smaller unrelated intent default; when no finite budget can make the response useful the envelope recommends an explicit unbounded or narrower query instead of a futile number; the emitted CLI, SDK, and MCP recovery bindings are executed and prove monotonic progress for default, intent, legacy, and explicit budgets; contracts, activity, history, graph, health, and every other non-resumable bounded producer are covered by a generated corpus; a seeded smaller-budget recommendation fails the recovery-reference assurance gate; repeated recovery either returns the requested complete projection or emits a strictly stronger, honest next action without cycles.
Guarantee every non-resumable output-budget recovery increases the effective capacity enough to make progress or explicitly recommends an unbounded/query-narrowing alternative
Agents never spend another turn following a recovery command that is provably weaker than the request that failed
The defect is reproducible on the current 2026.8.22 CLI after the general executable-recovery feature closed, making it a concrete recurrence and a gap in the producer-derived recovery corpus.
